title: The version of the app at the bottom of the Menu
why: Coach Milan 20 November 10:19: the version is one more tap away, in About, and not in the best place; put it in the Menu, between the menu block and Sign out.

opportunity.job: As a tester or Coach Milan, see which version I run at a glance, when I report something or check a release.
opportunity.kind: Slow: the version sits inside About, one tap further.
opportunity.why_now: Releases come several a day, and testers report against a version.

problem: To see which version runs, I open the Menu, scroll to About and open it. The version is the last line there.
story: When I open the Menu, I want to see the version at its bottom, so that I know which release I am on without one more tap.

ac.title: In the Menu
ac.text: Given the Menu, when I scroll to its bottom, then under the line Who's behind it · Impressum · Privacy notice · Disclaimer it says Version and the number, then the commit, as About says it.

ac.title: Above Sign out
ac.text: Given I am signed in, when I see the bottom of the Menu, then the version line sits between the links and Sign out.

ac.title: The release it is
ac.text: Given the app of a release, when I read the version line, then it is that release's number and commit, the same as in About.

unchanged: The links line and Sign out.
short: The version line under the links at the bottom of the Menu
rel: Proposed; not agreed until Coach Milan says Go
boardTitle: DT331: the version of the app at the bottom of the Menu
now: The version is the last line of About, one tap away from the Menu.
proposed: The same line, Version and the number · the commit, at the bottom of the Menu, under the links, above Sign out. About keeps it too.
decision: Open. Drawn for Coach Milan's Go.
details: The pictures are the real app, all from one scratch build of 0.3.167 with the line, not committed, built with the commit as the live app shows it (d1b274d). A local run has no sign-in and no commit, so the scratch shows Sign out as a signed-in phone has it, and the commit as a release has it.
Preview and production look the same: both show the release number and its commit. Only a build made on a computer without its commit says preview there.
The line in small muted text, as the links above it.
